what: Avery Dennison makes the labels and tags that go on things: pressure-sensitive label material sold in rolls to printers, and the price tags, care labels and radio-frequency tags that retailers put on clothing.
customers: Label printers and converters, consumer goods companies, and clothing retailers tagging their stock.
money: label stock, adhesives and films sold to converters
apparel tags, care labels and RFID inlays
moat: A coating and converting footprint close to customers worldwide, and in RFID a tag business where it supplies most of the clothing industry's volume.
risks: Revenue has been flat around $8.9B for four years
Label demand tracks consumer goods volumes, which have been soft
opportunities: $1.0B of free cash flow against a $13.8B market value, so about 13 times cash flow
RFID tagging is spreading from clothing into groceries, logistics and food safety, and Avery supplies most of the tags
Analysts see about 11% upside and the dividend has been raised for decades
watch: RFID tag volumes and whether label volumes return to growth.
